name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that the Pretrial Fairness Act is constitutional and does not unduly infringe on judicial authority, and that the lower court's indefinite detention of the petitioner was unlawful.

name: JUSTICE NEVILLE
description: Concurred, argued that Spencer's 100-year sentence is not a de facto life sentence due to parole eligibility after 20 years, but he can still bring an as-applied challenge in postconviction proceedings.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the equitable doctrine of laches should not apply to bar the claims and the court should address the complaint on its merits to ensure legislative redistricting plans conform with the Illinois Constitution.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: O'BRIEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the police officer's actions constituted an unreasonable warrantless search, and the evidence should have been suppressed.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred with the majority's reasoning and conclusions regarding constitutional violations but dissented on the majority's reliance on the lockstep doctrine, arguing that the court should interpret the Illinois Constitution independently.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that while a blind guilty plea does not waive sentencing challenges, the petitioner's 40-year sentence was proportionate to the offense and did not violate the proportionate penalties clause.

name: Justice Rochford
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that section 1(f) is a statute of repose, section 1.1 applies prospectively, and this application does not violate due process because the defendant's right to a defense accrues when the injury is discovered, not when exposure occurs.

name: JUSTICE OVERSTREET
description: Concurred, argued that warrantless arrests based on probable cause, even via investigative alerts, do not violate the Illinois Constitution, and the sentencing court properly considered juvenile factors.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's opinion legalizes investigative alerts, making warrantless arrests without judicial oversight official policy, which violates constitutional rights and has a racially discriminatory impact.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the officer-suit exception applies only to prospective injunctive relief, not to claims for monetary awards to redress past wrongs, which fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Claims.

name: Justice Neville
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act did not diminish constitutionally protected pension benefits or constitute a taking of private property, as the ability to vote for local pension board members and control fund investments are not protected benefits, and the Act does not impact monetary pension payments.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's exemptions do not violate equal protection or special legislation, and that plaintiffs waived their second amendment claim and failed to cross-appeal on the three-readings claim.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Dissented, argued that the court should have considered the three-readings rule violation, which renders the Act unconstitutional in its entirety, thereby obviating the need to address firearm restrictions.

name: JUSTICE OVERSTREET
description: Dissented, joined JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE's opinion that the Act should be found unconstitutional due to the three-readings rule violation.

name: JUSTICE O'BRIEN
description: Dissented, argued that the classifications in the legislation do not further its claimed purpose and thus violate the special legislation provision of the state constitution, finding plaintiffs are similarly situated to the exempted groups.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's pretrial release provisions are constitutional and do not violate the bail clause, crime victims' rights clause, or separation of powers clause.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that the majority failed to adequately address the defendants' affirmative defense regarding plaintiffs' standing, but ultimately agreed with the constitutionality of the Act.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the Act's abolishment of monetary bail directly violates the plain language of the constitution's bill of rights, specifically the vested rights of crime victims, and that the legislature impermissibly usurped the people's sovereign power.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the court's emergency orders tolling the speedy-trial statute were a valid exercise of its constitutional authority over court procedure and did not violate the separation-of-powers clause.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that defendant did not receive ineffective assistance of counsel as his attorney's performance was not deficient and he failed to show prejudice, and that a defendant does not have a constitutional right to be present during juror challenges.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred, argued that while Brown did not show ineffective assistance of counsel, hearings to exercise juror challenges are a critical stage of a trial where a defendant has a constitutional right to be present.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that counsel was deficient in agreeing to a procedure where defendant was not present for juror challenges, but affirmed because defendant failed to show prejudice.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Concurred with Justice O'Brien's special concurrence.

name: GARMAN JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the safe roads amendment applies to all transportation-related revenues, including those from home-rule units, and that the County's interpretation is unreasonable.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Dissented, argued that the majority failed to harmonize the safe roads amendment with home-rule provisions, and that extrinsic evidence shows the amendment was not intended to limit home-rule units' spending power.

name: OVERSTREET JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the complete failure to administer a trial oath to the jury is structural error, requiring automatic reversal because it deprives the defendant of a basic protection guaranteed by the state constitution and threatens the integrity of the judicial process.

name: Connors
description: Dissented, argued that the circuit court's admonishments and inquiries during voir dire were insufficient to cure the failure to administer a trial oath, which is structural error requiring automatic reversal.

name: GARMAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the City's ordinance definitions were inconsistent with the Act and prior judicial interpretations, and that legislative acquiescence makes judicial construction part of the statute.

name: JUSTICE CARTER
description: Concurred, argued that the appellate court improperly found the petitioner's sentence unconstitutional without a sufficiently developed evidentiary record and that the actual innocence claim requires reconsideration in light of new precedent.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred in remanding the actual innocence claim but dissented from remanding the proportionate penalties clause claim, arguing it is a facial challenge that should be rejected based on Harris and that the age line for criminal responsibility is a legislative policy determination.

name: Justice Michael J. Burke
description: Concurred in remanding the actual innocence claim but dissented from remanding the proportionate penalties clause claim, arguing the defendant failed to make a substantial showing of a constitutional violation and that the determination of a sentencing line between juveniles and adults is a matter of legislative policy.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, joining Justice Michael J. Burke's opinion.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the search for child pornography was lawful under the Fourth Amendment because the original warrant, though partially resolved by acquittal for sexual assault, still authorized a search for unauthorized video recording, and the child pornography was found in plain view during a search reasonably directed at that remaining purpose.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that the search violated McCavitt's constitutional and statutory rights because the July 24, 2013, search warrant was void 96 hours after its issuance, and McCavitt's acquittal restored his right to the immediate return of his property, making any subsequent search illegal.

name: THEIS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the firearm and ammunition tax ordinances violate the uniformity clause of the Illinois Constitution because the government failed to establish a substantial relationship between the tax classification and the object of the legislation, especially since it burdens a fundamental right.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's analysis is problematic because it leaves open the possibility for a future, more narrowly tailored tax on firearms and ammunition, which would still violate the Illinois Constitution's provision that the right to bear arms is subject only to police power, not taxation.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE ANNE M. BURKE
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the venue provision is constitutional because the offense of identity theft can be deemed committed where the victim's intangible identifying information is 'located'.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Recused from the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE GARMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully prolonged in violation of the Fourth Amendment, leading to the reversal of Bass's conviction and remand for a new trial, and vacated the appellate court's opinion on investigative alerts.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding that defendant's arrest violated article I, section 6 of the Illinois Constitution, arguing it was a valid alternative ground.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding on the unconstitutionality of investigative alerts under the Illinois Constitution, arguing for constitutional scrutiny of such alerts.
